common.faultInjection: The harness requests response loss; the common oracle consumes the response-loss fault exactly once per semantic operation. Candidate-native attempt counters are evidence only and do not decide which request is faulted.
rules: Do not change oracle semantics per candidate
Do not infer exactly-once for arbitrary external I/O
Preserve semantic operation identity across retries/restarts
Reject identity drift by checking total related external effects across all operation IDs
Record runtime/package/container identities for every run

forbidden: Node 26 until Temporal.Now replay behavior is resolved and regression-tested
workflow use of nondeterministic wall-clock APIs outside SDK-safe APIs

profiles.provenanceNote: Static source review is against GitHub release tag v4.27. First executable run must record npm lockfile integrity and verify the used APIs against the installed 4.27.6 artifact before candidate evidence is accepted.

runtimePolicy.database: PostgreSQL; exact image/version must be recorded at execution time

profiles.haConstraint: Automatic multi-process recovery must explicitly state whether DBOS Conductor or an equivalent executor-recovery mechanism is present

profiles.licenseConstraint: Restate server v1.7.8 is BSL 1.1; SDK is MIT. License acceptance is a separate gate from technical correctness.

profiles.t7Constraint: Current Trigger.dev v4.5.15 documentation states that a CRASHED run means the worker process crashed and will not be retried. managed-controller mode only tests controller restart plus response-loss recovery; it MUST NOT be counted as T7 worker-SIGKILL evidence. A direct self-hosted worker crash hook is required before T7 can receive PASS or FAIL from this laboratory.
